answer: Entry is priced like a congested harbor. Each new identity must burn a one-time fee into an address derived from its key and the epoch beacon, and the fee is set by an auction counting keys entering the same district in the last window: a gentle zephyr of newcomers pays little, while a sudden tide of a thousand keys lifts the price until renting them costs more than they can earn. Every burn is unrecoverable and bound to a distinct key, so a farm cannot amortize one payment across a garden of clones; it funds each at the raised rate, and the district quota stays shut until the crowd thins.
